title: Cultural-heritage protection is becoming more measurable, but public investment remains sharply uneven across places
source_unit: UNESCO Institute for Statistics, Culture 2026 Data Release and SDG 11.4.1 heritage-expenditure indicators
geography: Reporting countries and SDG regions, with 2024 or latest available per-capita public expenditure on cultural and natural heritage

observations.period: 2020-2025 survey cycles; country capacity to report SDG 11.4.1

denominator.unit: countries in the latest UIS expenditure survey cycle

initial_cycle.unit: countries responding in the initial 2020 survey cycle

latest_cycle.unit: countries responding in the latest UIS survey cycle

reporting_expansion.unit: times as many responding countries as in the initial cycle, approximately

observations.method: UIS compilation from the 2025 Survey of Expenditure on Cultural and Natural Heritage, tracking SDG 11.4.1 and its funding, heritage-type, and government-level disaggregations.
observations.uncertainty: More reporting improves visibility but does not make the 92-country frame globally complete; country definitions, reference years, price conversions, and missing data affect comparability.
observations.subgroup: National and local cultural authorities, heritage institutions, public and private funders, communities, and places whose preservation depends on measurable investment.
observations.counterinterpretation: Expanded reporting capacity can reflect statistical improvement rather than more actual investment or stronger preservation outcomes.

observations.period: 2024 or latest available year; public expenditure per person on cultural and natural heritage

regional_median.unit: PPP dollars constant 2017 median per person in Europe and Northern America among countries with available data

country_range.unit: PPP dollars constant 2017 per person across countries with available data

within_region_range.unit: PPP dollars constant 2017 per person within Europe and Northern America

observations.method: UIS comparison of public expenditure on preservation, protection, and conservation of cultural and natural heritage using SDG 11.4.1 data.
observations.uncertainty: The data release explicitly advises focusing on trends rather than treating the median as a complete welfare or preservation measure; spending is not equivalent to access, quality, or community control.
observations.subgroup: Heritage-dependent communities, cultural and natural heritage sites, public agencies, local governments, and residents facing unequal cultural-resource provision.
observations.counterinterpretation: Low per-capita public spending may coexist with private, community, philanthropic, or in-kind preservation efforts that are not captured by this indicator.

observations.period: 2021-2024; direction of per-capita public heritage-preservation investment

denominator.unit: countries with comparable 2021 and 2024 or latest-available expenditure data

countries_increasing.unit: percent of countries reporting increased investment in 2024 relative to 2021

countries_decreasing.unit: percent of countries not in the reported increase group, including countries with decreased investment or other movement

post_pandemic_pattern.value: contrasting increases and decreases across countries and SDG regions after the COVID-19 pandemic

observations.method: UIS comparison of changes in per-capita public spending on cultural and natural heritage preservation between 2021 and 2024 or latest available years.
observations.uncertainty: The source reports the increase share and contrasting regional trends but does not provide a causal explanation for each country's change or a direct measure of preservation outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Cultural and natural heritage agencies, local communities, public budgets, tourism and education systems, and places recovering from pandemic-era disruption.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher spending can reflect reconstruction, price changes, emergency repair, or accounting shifts rather than a durable expansion of cultural access or stewardship.

disaggregations.value: funding source, type of heritage, and level of government

policy_use.value: updated national data support monitoring progress toward preserving cultural and natural heritage

visibility_signal.value: culture becomes a budget and infrastructure question when expenditure is made comparable across places and government levels

observations.method: The UIS release combines indicator updates, funding and government-level disaggregation, and regional comparison to make cultural-heritage investment more visible in development monitoring.
observations.uncertainty: Comparable expenditure indicators reveal resource patterns but do not measure cultural meaning, participation, resilience, heritage condition, or whether communities control decisions.
observations.subgroup: Public funders, heritage custodians, cultural workers, Indigenous and local communities, residents, visitors, and future generations relying on preserved cultural and natural assets.
observations.counterinterpretation: Standardized indicators can improve accountability while also privileging what is countable and underrepresenting informal care, living heritage, and contested priorities.

related_sources.claim: UIS data browser for SDG 11.4.1 and cultural statistics.
UIS supporting documentation and background information for SDG 11.4.1 statistics.

boundary: This record adds a cultural-public-finance and measurement-capacity route linking heritage spending, regional inequality, post-pandemic budget direction, data visibility, and public stewardship. It is not a complete global spending census, a measure of heritage condition or cultural participation, respondent-level cultural behavior, causal preservation evaluation, or proof that spending produces equitable access or community control.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official UNESCO UIS Culture 2026 Data Release and linked UIS data resources were reviewed for the 30-to-92 reporting-country expansion, expenditure range, Europe-and-Northern-America median and internal range, 57% increase share, disaggregations, and trend-versus-level caveat.
